questions.topic: Eastern West Khasi Hills district formation
questions.q: Eastern West Khasi Hills District was carved out of which former district when it was inaugurated on 10 November 2021?
questions.e: The district administration records that Eastern West Khasi Hills was carved out of the erstwhile West Khasi Hills District and inaugurated on 10 November 2021. It was created by upgrading the Mairang Civil Sub-division.
tags: Eastern West Khasi Hills district formation

questions.topic: Eastern West Khasi Hills geographic coordinates
questions.q: Which coordinate range correctly describes the location of Eastern West Khasi Hills District?
questions.e: The district portal gives its latitude as 25 degrees 10 minutes to 25 degrees 51 minutes north and longitude as 91 degrees 10 minutes to 91 degrees 50 minutes east. These are the district's geographic ranges, not the coordinates of one town.
tags: Eastern West Khasi Hills geographic coordinates

questions.q: According to the district administration, which district lies to the north-east of Eastern West Khasi Hills?
questions.e: The official district description lists Ri Bhoi on the north-east, East Khasi Hills on the east, South West Khasi Hills on the south and West Khasi Hills on the west. The direction in the question is therefore decisive.

questions.q: At approximately what elevation above sea level does the Eastern West Khasi Hills district portal place Mairang?
questions.e: The district's topographical details give Mairang an elevation of 1,564 metres above sea level. This is the town's stated elevation, not the average elevation of every part of the district.

questions.q: The Publication and Reference section of Meghalaya's Directorate of Economics and Statistics prepares reports using information collected from which sources?
o: State and Central Government departments, autonomous bodies and semi-government agencies
Only village councils and municipal boards
Only the Reserve Bank of India
questions.e: The DES says it collects secondary data from State and Central Government departments, autonomous bodies and semi-government agencies. It compiles and analyses the information for publications such as the Statistical Handbook and Statistical Abstract.

questions.e: The DES Portal records 55 C&RD Blocks for reference year 2022. The reference year matters: this is a dated statistical figure and should not be presented as a newly verified 2026 administrative count.

questions.topic: Pa Togan Nengminja Sangma's last major resistance
questions.q: Where did the British expedition face the last major Garo resistance led by Pa Togan Nengminja Sangma in December 1837?
questions.e: The Meghalaya Government's Williamnagar account places the last major Garo resistance at Rongrenggiri. Pa Togan Nengminja Sangma was killed at Chisobibra near Rongrenggiri on 12 December 1837.

questions.q: At which Jowai location did U Kiang Nangbah take the oath to lead the Jaintia people in their struggle against British rule in 1861?
questions.e: The Meghalaya Government's Jowai history account identifies Madiah Kmai Blai as the field where Jaintia leaders met in 1861 and U Kiang Nangbah took the oath to lead the struggle. The place is distinct from the later site of his execution.

questions.q: On which date was U Kiang Nangbah publicly hanged at Iawmusiang in Jowai?
questions.e: The official Jowai account records that U Kiang Nangbah was publicly hanged at Iawmusiang, Jowai, on 30 December 1862 after a summary trial. His capture had occurred three days earlier, on 27 December 1862.

questions.q: According to the Meghalaya Government's account, when did the Jaintia resistance finally end after U Kiang Nangbah's death?
questions.e: The account says fighting continued after U Kiang Nangbah's execution and ended on 14 December 1863, when the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal removed the Special Commission and its power from the hilly Jaintia areas.

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 76 — tax collected but not paid
questions.q: A person collects an amount from a customer as representing GST but does not remit it. Under Section 76, which statement is correct even if the underlying supply is later found non-taxable?
o: The amount may always be retained if the supply was exempt
The collected amount must be paid forthwith to Government
The amount becomes input tax credit automatically
The amount is payable only after a criminal conviction
questions.e: Section 76 requires a person who collected an amount as representing tax and did not pay it to Government to pay it forthwith. The obligation applies irrespective of whether the underlying supplies were taxable, so the collection cannot be justified merely by later claiming exemption.
tags: CGST Act Section 76 — tax collected but not paid

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 77(1) — intra-State wrongly treated supply
questions.q: A registered person paid CGST and SGST on a transaction treated as intra-State, but the transaction is later held to be inter-State. What relief does Section 77(1) provide?
o: Refund of the Central and State taxes paid, subject to prescribed manner and conditions
Automatic waiver of every tax liability for the financial year
A refund of only the State tax, with no Central tax adjustment
A permanent exemption from IGST registration
questions.e: Section 77(1) addresses tax paid under the wrong intra-State classification when the supply is later held to be inter-State. It provides for refund of the Central and State tax so paid, in the prescribed manner and subject to prescribed conditions.
tags: CGST Act Section 77(1) — intra-State wrongly treated supply

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 78 — ordinary payment period
questions.q: After service of an order under the CGST Act, what is the ordinary period within which the taxable person must pay the amount before recovery proceedings are initiated under Section 78?
questions.e: Section 78 ordinarily allows three months from the date of service of the order for payment. The proviso permits the proper officer, for reasons recorded in writing and in the interest of revenue, to require payment within a shorter specified period.

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 85 — transfer of business
questions.q: A taxable person transfers an entire business by sale while tax dues relating to the period before transfer remain unpaid. Who is liable under Section 85(1)?
o: Only the transferee, and only after a fresh assessment
The transferor and transferee jointly and severally, to the extent of the transfer
Neither party once the sale deed is registered
questions.e: Section 85(1) makes the taxable person and the person to whom the business is transferred jointly and severally liable for tax, interest or penalty due up to the time of transfer, whether determined before transfer or determined later. Liability extends wholly or to the extent of the transfer.
tags: CGST Act Section 85 — transfer of business

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 86 — agent and principal
questions.q: An agent supplies taxable goods on behalf of a principal. Which parties are jointly and severally liable for the tax payable on those goods under Section 86?
questions.e: Section 86 covers an agent who supplies or receives taxable goods on behalf of a principal. Both agent and principal are jointly and severally liable for the tax payable on those goods; the provision should not be casually extended to every service transaction.
tags: CGST Act Section 86 — agent and principal

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 87 — retrospective merger date
questions.q: Two companies merge under an order that takes effect from a date earlier than the order itself. For the intervening period, the companies made supplies to each other. How are those transactions treated under Section 87(1)?
o: They are ignored because the merger date is retrospective
They are included in the respective companies' turnover of supply or receipt and taxed accordingly
They are treated only as exempt branch transfers
They are shifted entirely to the transferee's turnover after the order
questions.e: Section 87(1) requires supplies and receipts between the companies during the period from the earlier effective date to the date of the order to be included in the respective companies' turnover. This prevents the intervening transactions from disappearing merely because the merger order operates retrospectively.
tags: CGST Act Section 87 — retrospective merger date

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 88 — liquidator's first intimation
questions.q: A liquidator is appointed when a company is being wound up. Within what period must the liquidator intimate the Commissioner of the appointment under Section 88(1)?
questions.e: Section 88(1) requires the liquidator to give intimation of the appointment to the Commissioner within thirty days after appointment. The Commissioner then has a separate period of three months from receipt of the intimation to notify the liquidator of the amount considered sufficient for tax, interest or penalty.

questions.q: A partner retires from a firm that has GST dues. The retirement date is not intimated to the Commissioner within one month. Until when does the retiring partner's liability under the first proviso to Section 90 continue?
o: Only up to the date of the retirement deed
Until the firm files its next annual return
Until the intimation is received by the Commissioner
questions.e: Section 90 keeps the retiring partner liable for dues up to the retirement date. If the required written intimation is not given within one month from retirement, the partner's liability under the first proviso continues until the Commissioner receives the intimation.

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 93 — death and discontinued business
questions.q: A taxable person dies and the business is discontinued. Under Section 93(1)(b), how far is the legal representative liable for the deceased person's GST dues?
o: Without limit from the legal representative's own property
Only out of the deceased's estate and to the extent that the estate can meet the charge
Only for dues assessed before death
No liability arises if the business has stopped
questions.e: Where the business is discontinued, Section 93(1)(b) makes the legal representative liable out of the deceased person's estate, limited to the extent the estate is capable of meeting the charge. The provision covers dues determined before death but unpaid and dues determined after death.
tags: CGST Act Section 93 — death and discontinued business

questions.q: Which constitutional provision empowers Parliament to form an autonomous State within Assam and provide it with a legislature, a Council of Ministers, or both?
questions.e: Article 244A authorises Parliament, by law, to form an autonomous State within Assam comprising specified tribal areas and to provide for a legislature, a Council of Ministers, or both. It is distinct from the ordinary creation of a new State under Article 3.

questions.q: Article 275(1) provides for grants-in-aid from the Union to States, including special provision for which purpose?
o: Promoting the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas
Paying salaries of all municipal councillors
questions.e: Article 275(1) authorises grants-in-aid to States and includes provision for sums needed to meet the costs of schemes for promoting the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas. These are constitutional grants, not a direct tax-devolution formula.

questions.topic: Article 338A — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
questions.q: Which constitutional body is established under Article 338A?
questions.e: Article 338A provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. Its constitutional role includes investigating and monitoring safeguards for Scheduled Tribes, inquiring into specific complaints and advising on their socio-economic development.

questions.q: Under Article 339(1), who may appoint a Commission to report on the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: Article 339(1) empowers the President to appoint a Commission to report on the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes in the States. It concerns Union oversight and is distinct from the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A.

questions.topic: Article 312 — creation of All India Services
questions.q: What special Rajya Sabha resolution is required before Parliament may create a new All India Service under Article 312?
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
A majority of the total membership of both Houses
A resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting
A unanimous resolution of all State Legislatures
questions.e: Article 312 requires the Council of States to declare by a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest to create one or more All India Services. Parliament may then provide for their creation by law.
tags: Article 312 — creation of All India Services

questions.q: After the President issues a public notification specifying Scheduled Tribes for a State or Union Territory under Article 342, who may include or exclude a community from that list?
o: The State Cabinet by executive order
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes by recommendation alone
questions.e: Article 342(2) reserves the power to include or exclude a community from the notified list of Scheduled Tribes to Parliament by law. A State executive order or a Commission recommendation by itself cannot amend the constitutional list.

questions.q: If the Reserve Bank wants to inject durable liquidity into the banking system through an open market operation, which action is appropriate?
o: Selling Government securities in the market
Buying Government securities from the market
Increasing the face value of currency notes
Reducing the statutory audit period of banks
questions.e: An RBI purchase of Government securities injects durable liquidity because payment for the securities adds funds to the banking system. A sale absorbs liquidity. Open market operations are outright purchases or sales, distinct from short-term repo transactions.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Open Market Operations and CRR.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Open Market Operations and CRR

questions.q: In the RBI's liquidity adjustment framework, which facility serves as the floor of the liquidity corridor?
questions.e: The RBI describes the Standing Deposit Facility as the floor of the liquidity corridor. It allows the RBI to absorb liquidity without providing collateral, while the Marginal Standing Facility is an overnight borrowing facility above the policy repo rate.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Liquidity Operations, SDF and MSF.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Liquidity Operations, SDF and MSF

questions.q: A scheduled bank faces a temporary overnight liquidity shortage and seeks to borrow from the RBI at a rate above the policy repo rate. Which facility is designed for this purpose?
questions.e: The Marginal Standing Facility is an overnight borrowing facility for eligible banks at a rate above the policy repo rate. It is not the same as the Standing Deposit Facility, which absorbs liquidity and forms the corridor floor.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Liquidity Operations, SDF and MSF.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Liquidity Operations, SDF and MSF

questions.q: Which institution is designated under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 as the authority for regulating and supervising payment systems in India?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
National Payments Corporation of India acting as the statutory regulator
questions.e: The RBI's official FAQ explains that the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 provides the legal framework for regulation and supervision of payment systems and designates the Reserve Bank as the authority. NPCI operates several retail payment systems but is not the statutory regulator under the Act.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Payment and Settlement Systems Act FAQ, updated 20 October 2025.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India — Payment and Settlement Systems Act FAQ, updated 20 October 2025

questions.q: What does the word 'gross' signify in Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS)?
o: All transactions are settled together at the end of the month
Each transfer is settled individually rather than being offset against other transfers
Only cash deposits are settled in real time
Transactions are settled only after a clearing-house netting cycle
questions.e: In RTGS, each payment instruction is settled individually on a real-time basis. Gross settlement contrasts with net settlement, in which multiple obligations are offset and only the net amount is settled. The RBI FAQ describes RTGS as a gross settlement system.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Reserve Bank of India — Payment and Settlement Systems Act FAQ, updated 20 October 2025.

questions.q: Moist air is forced to rise over a mountain barrier, cools as it expands and produces rain on the windward slope. Which process is being described?
questions.e: Orographic rainfall occurs when relief forces moist air upward. As the air rises, it expands and cools adiabatically; water vapour condenses and precipitation is produced, often leaving a comparatively drier rain-shadow region on the leeward side.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography

questions.q: On a sunny afternoon, wind blows from the sea towards the land. Which pressure pattern most directly explains this sea breeze?
o: The sea heats faster and develops lower pressure
The land heats faster, air rises and surface pressure becomes relatively lower over land
The land cools faster and draws air from the sea
The Coriolis force creates a permanent high-pressure belt over the coast
questions.e: Land generally heats more quickly than the sea during the day. Air over the warmer land rises, producing relatively lower surface pressure; cooler air from the sea moves inland to replace it, creating a sea breeze.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography

questions.q: Which atmospheric condition is called a temperature inversion?
o: Air temperature decreases with height at the normal environmental lapse rate
Air temperature increases with height through a layer of the atmosphere
Air pressure remains identical at every altitude
The atmosphere contains no water vapour
questions.e: A temperature inversion is a layer in which temperature increases with altitude rather than decreasing. It suppresses vertical mixing, so pollutants and fog may remain trapped close to the ground beneath the inversion layer.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography

questions.q: A river meander becomes increasingly narrow at its neck and is eventually cut off from the main channel. What landform may remain?
questions.e: When erosion narrows a meander neck and the river cuts through it, deposition may seal the former loop. The abandoned curved channel becomes an oxbow lake, a feature associated with river deposition and lateral erosion on floodplains.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography.

questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Geography

questions.q: In a nephron, blood is filtered under pressure at the glomerulus. Into which structure does the initial filtrate pass?
questions.e: The glomerulus is a capillary tuft where ultrafiltration occurs. Water and small dissolved substances pass through the filtration barrier into Bowman's capsule, while blood cells and most large plasma proteins remain in the blood.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science

questions.q: Antidiuretic hormone activity increases the reabsorption of water in which part of the nephron?
questions.e: Antidiuretic hormone increases the permeability of parts of the distal nephron and collecting ducts to water, allowing more water to be reabsorbed. Reduced ADH action therefore produces a larger volume of dilute urine.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science

questions.q: Why can prolonged iodine deficiency lead to enlargement of the thyroid gland?
o: Iodine is required for synthesis of thyroid hormones, and deficiency can stimulate thyroid enlargement
Iodine directly converts glucose into insulin
Iodine is the main structural component of red blood cells
Iodine prevents the kidney from filtering urea
questions.e: The thyroid gland requires iodine to synthesise thyroxine and related thyroid hormones. When iodine intake is insufficient, hormone production falls and compensatory stimulation can enlarge the gland, producing goitre.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science

questions.q: When a nerve impulse reaches the terminal of a neuron, how is the signal commonly transmitted across a chemical synapse to the next cell?
o: By a continuous strand of cytoplasm joining the neurons
By neurotransmitter molecules released into the synaptic cleft
By red blood cells carrying the impulse
By changing the DNA sequence of the next neuron
questions.e: At a chemical synapse, the arriving impulse triggers release of neurotransmitter molecules from the presynaptic terminal. These chemicals diffuse across the synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on the next cell, initiating a response.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science

questions.q: A young shoot bends towards a window. Which explanation best describes the role of auxin in this response?
o: Auxin accumulates on the illuminated side and stops all growth
Auxin accumulates more on the shaded side, causing greater cell elongation there
Auxin destroys the shoot tip on the shaded side
Auxin converts the shoot into a root
questions.e: In a shoot exposed to directional light, auxin becomes more concentrated on the shaded side. Cells there elongate more than cells on the illuminated side, causing the shoot to bend towards the light; this is positive phototropism.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the role of bile in digestion?
o: Bile contains the main enzyme that breaks proteins into amino acids
Bile emulsifies large fat globules into smaller droplets but is not itself a digestive enzyme
Bile converts starch directly into glucose
Bile is produced by the pancreas and stored in the kidney
questions.e: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder. Bile salts emulsify large fat globules into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area available to lipase; bile itself is not a digestive enzyme.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science

questions.q: Which group of coastal ecosystems is commonly associated with the term 'blue carbon'?
o: Mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass meadows
Glaciers, rocky cliffs and sand dunes
questions.e: Blue carbon refers to biologically driven carbon storage in coastal and marine systems, especially rooted vegetation such as mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrasses. Their biomass and sediments can store substantial carbon over long periods.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. IPCC — Sixth Assessment Report, Synthesis Report Glossary.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: IPCC — Sixth Assessment Report, Synthesis Report Glossary

questions.q: A town builds flood-resilient drainage and raises critical facilities to cope with more intense rainfall. This is primarily an example of which climate response?
o: Mitigation, because it directly removes carbon dioxide
Adaptation, because it adjusts to expected climate impacts
Carbon accounting, because it measures emissions
Geoengineering, because it changes the Earth's orbit
questions.e: Climate adaptation involves adjustment to actual or expected climate and its effects to moderate harm or exploit opportunities. Flood-resilient drainage responds to the consequences of climate change; mitigation instead reduces greenhouse-gas emissions or enhances sinks.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. IPCC — Sixth Assessment Report, Synthesis Report Glossary.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: IPCC — Sixth Assessment Report, Synthesis Report Glossary

questions.q: A persistent pollutant becomes more concentrated in organisms at successively higher trophic levels of a food chain. What is this process called?
questions.e: Biomagnification describes an increase in pollutant concentration at higher trophic levels. Bioaccumulation is different: it refers to the build-up of a substance within an individual organism over time from its surroundings and food.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NCERT — Official Online Textbooks, Biology and Science

questions.q: Which of the following is best classified as a regulating ecosystem service rather than a provisioning service?
o: Collecting edible fruits from a forest
Wetlands reducing flood peaks and improving water quality
Gathering medicinal plants for household use
questions.e: Regulating services arise from the regulation of ecosystem processes, such as flood control, climate regulation, disease regulation and water purification. Timber, fruit and medicinal plants are examples of provisioning benefits obtained directly from ecosystems.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. IPCC — AR6 Working Group II Glossary.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: IPCC — AR6 Working Group II Glossary

questions.q: A department rents virtual machines, storage and networking from a cloud provider but installs and manages its own operating system and applications. Which cloud service model is this?
questions.e: Infrastructure as a Service supplies virtualised computing resources such as processing, storage and networking. The customer generally manages the operating system and deployed applications, while the provider manages the underlying physical infrastructure.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. NIELIT — Course on Computer Concepts Plus (CCC Plus).
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NIELIT — Course on Computer Concepts Plus (CCC Plus)

questions.q: A clerk has thousands of transaction rows and wants a quick summary of total collections by tax circle and month without changing the original records. Which spreadsheet feature is most suitable?
questions.e: A pivot table groups and summarises tabular data by selected fields. It can aggregate values such as totals or counts by tax circle and month while leaving the underlying source records intact.

questions.q: A spreadsheet cell should accept only dates within a specified financial year. Which feature is designed to restrict the type or range of values users may enter?
questions.e: Data validation applies rules to cell entries, such as allowing only dates within a defined range or numbers within specified limits. It helps prevent invalid input at the point of entry rather than merely highlighting errors afterwards.

questions.q: In a public-key infrastructure, what is the principal role of a trusted Certifying Authority when issuing a digital certificate?
o: To store every user's private key
To bind a verified identity to a public key in a digitally signed certificate
To guarantee that a document contains no spelling errors
To encrypt every file on the user's computer automatically
questions.e: A Certifying Authority verifies identity according to its certificate policy and digitally signs a certificate that binds the subject's identity to a public key. The private key remains with its holder; the CA does not need to take possession of it.

questions.q: A right circular cone is cut parallel to its base to form a frustum with larger radius 6 cm, smaller radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. What is its volume?
questions.e: The volume of a conical frustum is V = (πh/3)(R² + r² + Rr). Substituting h = 4, R = 6 and r = 3 gives (4π/3)(36 + 9 + 18) = (4π/3) × 63 = 84π cm³.

questions.topic: Combinations with at least one woman
questions.q: A committee of three is selected from five men and four women. How many different committees contain at least one woman?
questions.e: There are nine people in total, so unrestricted committees number C(9,3) = 84. Committees containing no woman are all-men committees: C(5,3) = 10. Therefore committees with at least one woman = 84 − 10 = 74.

questions.q: Five files A, B, C, D and E are arranged in a row. A is before B, C is after A but before B, B is immediately before D, and E is after D. Which file occupies the middle position?
questions.e: The constraints force A before C before B, followed immediately by D, with E after D. The only possible order is A–C–B–D–E, so C occupies the third, or middle, position.

questions.q: Three clerks A, B and C each make one statement about who filed first. A says, 'B filed first.' B says, 'I did not file first.' C says, 'A did not file first.' If exactly one statement is true, who filed first?
questions.e: If A filed first, A's statement is false, B's statement is true and C's statement is false: exactly one statement is true. If B filed first, A and C are both true; if C filed first, B and C are both true. Therefore A must have filed first.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct completion: 'The review committee recommended that the disputed entry ___ checked again before approval.'
questions.e: After verbs such as recommend, insist or demand, formal English commonly uses the mandative subjunctive: the base form of the verb. Therefore 'be checked' is correct, even though the subject is singular and the sentence refers to a future action.

questions.q: Which sentence maintains parallel grammatical structure?
o: The clerk was asked to record the date, verifying the amount and the receipt was attached.
The clerk was asked to record the date, verify the amount and attach the receipt.
The clerk was asked recording the date, to verify the amount and attaching the receipt.
The clerk was asked to record the date, the amount was verified and attaching the receipt.
questions.e: The three actions should appear in the same grammatical form after 'to': to record, verify and attach. The second option keeps the verbs parallel. The other options mix infinitives, participles and full clauses, making the series uneven.
